description:
FILED s421 (Fable review of s420's #413).  PRE-EXISTING (identical at
47e0750): #413 did not introduce it — it made the bare-name convention
explicit and extended it to qualified calls, which is what perl does.

    { package A; sub f($)  { "A:$_[0]" } }
    { package B; sub f(&@) { my $c=shift; "B:".$c->().":@_" } }
    package A; print f 1, 2; print "\n";     # perl A:12   PCL A:1
    package B; print f { "x" } 3, 4;         # perl B:x:3 4  PCL B:x:3 4
  reversed declaration order:
    { package C; sub h(&@) {...} } { package D; sub h($) {...} }
    print D::h 5, 6;          # perl D:56     PCL D:56
    print C::h { "y" } 7, 8;  # perl C:y:7 8  PCL DROPPED (Missing case: [)

Because `prototypes` is one flat hash keyed by the bare name, the LAST
registration wins for every package.

MEASURED s421 (same bare name, different prototypes, within ONE file):
perl-tests 0; lib/ 0; cpan-tests/modules 0; perl's t/: op/lexsub.t
(`foo` "" vs "$ネ" — a LEXICAL sub, different mechanism) and comp/redef.t
(same-package sequential redefinitions — perl's last-wins, no divergence).
Cross-FILE collisions (a module's exported prototype vs a same-named user
sub) NOT measured — use PCL_PROTO_ORACLE if that question comes up.

FIX SHAPE: key `prototypes` by (package, bare-name) with the bare table as
the fallback — `declared_subs` already carries the package and
`_bareword_callable_here` already knows the call site's package; register
under BOTH so unqualified lookups from other packages (imports) keep working.
Filler by the s366 filler-scope rule; no corpus row depends on it today.

CLOSED s427 (Opus), by the fix shape this task names.  perl's rule is the sub
it RESOLVES at compile time; a second table `pkg_prototypes`
({bare => {pkg => info}}) is filled at the Pl::Environment seam (the qualifier
when the name carries one, else the package the sub pre-scan already computes
for add_declared_sub, else the current package) and travels through merge()
and clone().

THE LOOKUP IS DELIBERATELY NARROW: the per-package table is consulted ONLY
when a bare name has more than one declaring package.  With 0 or 1 the flat
table IS that entry, so every non-colliding program takes exactly the path it
took before — corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files, emission-ab SAME=22 over
the lib shims, gate-SET scan over both populations shows no verdict moving for
this item.  The flat table stays the fallback when the current package has no
declaration of its own, because that is how an IMPORTED prototype reaches a
call site.

Both halves A/B'd on a 753ecab worktree: `package A; print f 1, 2` was A:1
(perl A:12) and is now A:12; `print C::h { "y" } 7, 8` was DROPPED and now
prints C:y:7 8.  Eight-shape probe identical to perl (imported first { } @n,
a qualified call from a package with its own f, unqualified resolution in the
current package, a qualified DECLARATION, same-package redefinition = last
wins, a third-package call, an unrelated two-arg prototype); the only
difference in the whole run is perl's two compile-time warnings, which PCL
does not emit (#221).  Guard Pl/t/prototype-01.t, 9 rows beside #413's.

RESIDUE for a future touch: a call site in a package with NO declaration of
its own still gets the last-registered entry when two OTHERS collide.  perl
would die "Undefined subroutine" there, so no working program can tell; if the
strict form is ever wanted, the seam is one line in Pl::Environment::_proto_entry.
title: The prototype table is keyed by the BARE sub name — two packages declaring the same sub name with DIFFERENT prototypes collide (last registration wins): a silent wrong in one order, a DROP in the other
